children: , a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of allogeneic CAR T (AlloCAR T) products for cancer and autoimmune disease, today announced its participation in the 68th American Society of Hematology (ASH) Annual Meeting and Exposition in New Orleans. Allogene’s activities at ASH will highlight the potential of allogeneic CAR T to expand patient access through new physician market research and expert discussions on barriers to treatment. Additionally, the Company’s pivotal ALPHA3 trial, evaluating cemacabtagene ansegedleucel (cema-cel) as minimal residual disease (MRD)-guided first-line consolidation therapy for patients with large B-cell lymphoma (LBCL), will be featured at a clinical trial showcase hosted by Natera.

“For too long, we've allowed the realities of the autologous CAR T delivery model to limit our vision of what's possible,” said Zachary Roberts, M.D., Ph.D., President and Chief Executive Officer of Allogene Therapeutics. “The time has come to change that. Our new physician research points to an opportunity that extends beyond overcoming today's stubborn access barriers. When physicians have an actionable treatment option, their willingness to test for MRD increases. When CAR T can potentially be delivered closer to patients, doors may open to broader adoption. With cema-cel and ALPHA3, we are pursuing both – bringing CAR T earlier in the treatment journey and potentially expanding where patients can receive it. At ASH, we want to challenge the industry to think bigger about what CAR T can become.”
CAR T for Real Life – Fixing What’s Broken with CAR T

Allogene will host an in-person event challenging conventional assumptions about when, where, and how CAR T can be delivered. The program will feature new market research from a survey of 152 hematologists and oncologists as well as a moderated panel of physicians to challenge current assumptions about CAR T delivery, explore the potential of MRD-guided intervention and community-based treatment, and discuss what it will take to translate these opportunities into clinical practice. The discussion will include a live audience Q&A.

ALPHA3: Pioneering MRD-Guided First-Line Consolidation in LBCL with Cema-Cel, an Allogeneic CAR T Built for Real-World Treatment

A Natera-hosted presentation will highlight the design and rationale of ALPHA3, the first registrational trial evaluating MRD-guided 1L consolidation in LBCL. The pivotal trial uses Natera’s patented phased variant technology to detect MRD after first line therapy. It evaluates cema-cel in patients who achieve remission following standard chemoimmunotherapy but remain at high risk of relapse, as identified by Natera’s CLARITY™ MRD assay.
David Kurtz, M.D., Ph.D., Natera, Inc.
Ernest N. Morial Convention Center, New Orleans – Hall J – Corporate Presentation Theater 6

Allogene Therapeutics, with headquarters in South San Francisco, is a clinical-stage biotechnology company pioneering the development of allogeneic chimeric antigen receptor T cell (AlloCAR T) products for cancer and autoimmune disease. Led by cell therapy veterans applying proven CAR T experience, Allogene is developing a pipeline of off-the-shelf CAR T cell product candidates with the goal of delivering readily available cell therapy on-demand, more reliably, and at greater scale to more patients. For more information, please visit www.allogene.com, and follow Allogene Therapeutics on X and LinkedIn.
